title: Introduction to Web Development & Setting up Environment

topics.title: Web Development Architecture: Client vs Server-Side & HTTP Request Lifecycle

intro.definition: Web development encompasses client-side presentation in the browser and server-side computing where scripts synthesize dynamic markup, query databases, and handle security.
intro.background: Static web pages were replaced in the 1990s by server-side scripting. Rasmus Lerdorf developed PHP in 1994, which combined with MySQL and Apache into the LAMP stack.
intro.importance: Separating client rendering from server logic guarantees security, transactional atomicity, and scalable architecture.
objectives: Trace HTTP request lifecycle from DNS to rendering.

fundamentals.concepts: Client code runs in the browser sandbox. Server code executes with full OS and database access on the backend server.

terminology.definition: Code executed in browser without direct database access.
Code compiled on web server prior to output delivery.
Stateless request-response protocol between client and server.
Linux, Apache, MySQL, and PHP software stack.

fundamentals.principles:
1. Statelessness: HTTP does not store conversational state.
2. Zero-Trust Client: Validate all inputs server-side.
fundamentals.structures: Client Browser <== HTTP ==> Apache Server <== FastCGI ==> PHP Zend Engine <== SQL ==> MySQL Server

sequence: 1. User enters URL or clicks submit.
2. Browser resolves DNS and establishes TCP handshake.
3. Browser transmits HTTP request header and body.
4. Apache routes .php requests to the Zend Engine.
5. Zend Engine executes bytecode and queries MySQL if needed.
6. Database returns relational recordsets.
7. PHP blends dynamic data into HTML markup.
8. Apache sends HTTP 200 response with HTML payload to browser.
detailed_explanation.code_architecture: query('SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = 1'); $student = $res->fetch_assoc(); ?>

important_points: Browser executes client-side presentation code.
PHP executes exclusively on the server before transmitting output.
HTTP is a stateless protocol.
Zend Engine compiles PHP into opcodes.
Client-side validation must always be backed by server validation.

revision.summary: Three-tier architecture separates browser presentation, server application logic, and database persistence.
revision.terminology: Client, Server, Zend Engine, HTTP, FastCGI, LAMP.
revision.mechanisms: Browser Req -> Apache -> PHP Compile -> MySQL -> Render -> HTTP 200.
revision.common_mistakes: Relying on browser JavaScript validation for data security.

topics.title: Development Environment Setup: Installation of XAMPP/WAMP, Apache, MySQL & PHP Configuration

intro.definition: A local development environment bundles Apache, MySQL, and PHP into an offline software package on a developer's desktop.
intro.background: Bundled distributions like XAMPP provide a single control panel to start and stop services without manual binary compilation.
intro.importance: Knowledge of port binding, document roots, and runtime php.ini directives is essential for troubleshooting setup issues.
objectives: Install and start Apache and MySQL.
Set up web root in htdocs.

fundamentals.concepts: Apache listens on port 80, MySQL on port 3306. Browser requests to localhost point to loopback IP 127.0.0.1.

terminology.definition: Public directory serving PHP and web assets in XAMPP.
Configuration file controlling PHP runtime execution limits.
Apache server configuration file governing ports and directories.

fundamentals.principles:
1. Unique Ports: Each network daemon requires an exclusive port.
2. Restart After Edit: php.ini changes require an Apache restart.

sequence: 1. Download and run XAMPP installer.
2. Start Apache and MySQL in XAMPP Control Panel.
3. If port 80 is blocked by IIS, change port to 8080 in httpd.conf.
4. Open http://localhost to verify Apache status.
5. Open http://localhost/phpmyadmin to manage MySQL.
6. Set upload_max_filesize = 32M in php.ini and restart Apache.
detailed_explanation.code_architecture:
# php.ini settings
display_errors = On
error_reporting = E_ALL
memory_limit = 256M
upload_max_filesize = 32M

examples.code:
<?php
echo 'PHP: ' . phpversion();
$m = @new mysqli('localhost', 'root', '');
echo $m->connect_error ? ' DB Error' : ' DB Connected';
?>

important_points: XAMPP bundles Apache, MySQL, and PHP into one folder.
Projects must be located in htdocs to be accessible via browser.
Port 80 conflicts can be resolved by changing port in httpd.conf.
Editing php.ini requires restarting Apache.
phpinfo() outputs comprehensive runtime information.

revision.summary: Local web servers simulate production environments. Configuration files manage memory, ports, and errors.
revision.mechanisms: Browser localhost -> Apache port 80 -> PHP parser -> MySQL 3306.
revision.common_mistakes: Forgetting to restart Apache after editing php.ini.

title: PHP Basics, Functions, Arrays and Strings

topics.title: PHP Syntax, Variables, Data Types, Type Juggling & Control Structures

intro.definition: PHP syntax supports procedural and object-oriented paradigms. Variables start with $ and are dynamically typed.
intro.background: PHP 7 and 8 introduced scalar type declarations and match expressions for strict computational evaluation.
intro.importance: Mastery of control flow, data types, and equality operators prevents logic bugs and security flaws.
objectives: Manipulate scalar and compound data types.
Use if-else, switch, and match constructs.

fundamentals.concepts: Variables are declared on assignment. Type juggling automatically coerces types during operations unless strict types are enabled.

terminology.definition: Automatic data type conversion by the runtime engine.
Compares both value and datatype without coercion.
PHP 8 expression returning values with strict comparison.

fundamentals.principles:
1. Favor Strict Equality: Always use === to prevent type coercion vulnerabilities.
2. Defend Boundaries: Ensure loop conditions terminate predictably.

sequence: 1. Parser encounters variable prefixed with $.
2. Type is dynamically allocated based on literal value.
3. Expressions evaluate with type coercion if operators differ.
4. Control structures branch based on boolean truthiness.
5. Foreach iterates through array key-value elements.

diagram.caption: Figure 2.1: PHP Type System & Flow Control
diagram.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 800 200' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='width:100%;height:auto;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #E5E9F1;'><rect x='30' y='30' width='220' height='140' rx='8' fill='#F7F8FC' stroke='#377FE6'/><text x='140' y='60' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='700' fill='#377FE6' text-anchor='middle'>Data Types</text><text x='50' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• int, float, string, bool</text><text x='50' y='110' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• array, object, null</text><rect x='290' y='30' width='220' height='140' rx='8' fill='#F7F8FC' stroke='#786CE5'/><text x='400' y='60' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='700' fill='#786CE5' text-anchor='middle'>Control Flow</text><text x='310' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• if / elseif / else</text><text x='310' y='110' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• switch & PHP 8 match</text><rect x='550' y='30' width='220' height='140' rx='8' fill='#F7F8FC' stroke='#28A994'/><text x='660' y='60' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='700' fill='#28A994' text-anchor='middle'>Loop Iteration</text><text x='570' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• while & do-while</text><text x='570' y='110' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='10' fill='#19283D'>• for & foreach ($a as $k=>$v)</text></svg>

important_points: PHP variables are prefixed with $ and dynamically typed.
Strict typing can be enforced using declare(strict_types=1).
The match expression replaces switch with strict checking.
Foreach is the standard tool for iterating associative arrays.
Null coalescing (??) provides clean default fallback values.

revision.summary: PHP variables and types are versatile. Strict typing ensures predictable application state.
revision.terminology: Type Juggling, Strict Types, Match Expression, Foreach.
revision.mechanisms: Lexer -> Type Coercion -> Branching Logic -> Execution.
revision.common_mistakes: Using loose == instead of strict === leading to logic bypasses.

topics.title: Functions in PHP: Scope, File Inclusion & Built-in Library

intro.definition: Functions package reusable code blocks. PHP supports typed arguments, return types, and pass-by-reference.
intro.background: Modular functions allow breaking large systems into isolated, testable modules across multiple files.
intro.importance: Understanding file inclusion prevents fatal errors and duplicated function declarations.
objectives: Declare functions with return type hints.
Compare include, require, include_once, and require_once.

fundamentals.concepts: Function variables have local scope. File inclusion imports external script statements directly into the calling script.

terminology.definition: Includes file once; triggers fatal E_COMPILE_ERROR if missing.
Includes file once; triggers non-fatal E_WARNING if missing.
Local variable retaining its value across function calls.

fundamentals.principles:
1. Critical Files: Always use require_once for database config.
2. DRY Code: Encapsulate shared routines into functions.
fundamentals.structures: function add(int $a, int $b): int { return $a + $b; } | require_once 'config.php';

sequence: 1. Script invokes require_once 'db.php'.
2. Engine verifies file has not been loaded previously.
3. Engine loads and compiles external file.
4. Function is invoked with parameter arguments.
5. Local stack frame created, value computed, and returned.
detailed_explanation.code_architecture:
<?php
function formatCurrency(float $val): string {
    return '₹' . number_format($val, 2);
}
echo formatCurrency(1499.5);
?>

diagram.caption: Figure 2.2: Comparison of File Inclusion Statements
diagram.svg: <svg viewBox='0 0 800 180' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='width:100%;height:auto;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #E5E9F1;'><rect x='40' y='30' width='330' height='120' rx='8' fill='#F7F8FC' stroke='#D65F64'/><text x='205' y='60' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='700' fill='#D65F64' text-anchor='middle'>require / require_once</text><text x='60' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#19283D'>• Fatal E_COMPILE_ERROR</text><text x='60' y='110' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#19283D'>• Halts script execution</text><rect x='430' y='30' width='330' height='120' rx='8' fill='#F7F8FC' stroke='#F2C75C'/><text x='595' y='60' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='12' font-weight='700' fill='#B38600' text-anchor='middle'>include / include_once</text><text x='450' y='90' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#19283D'>• Warning E_WARNING</text><text x='450' y='110' font-family='sans-serif' font-size='11' fill='#19283D'>• Continues execution</text></svg>

examples.code:
<?php
function hit() {
    static $c = 0;
    return ++$c;
}
echo hit() . ' ' . hit(); // 1 2
?>

important_points: `require_once` prevents duplicate declaration fatal crashes.
Functions can have strict parameter and return type declarations.
Static variables maintain their state across multiple calls.
Prefixing parameter with & passes it by reference.
Core math and string functions are globally accessible.

revision.summary: Modular programming in PHP uses functions and strict file inclusion statements.
revision.mechanisms: Path resolution -> Cache check -> Compilation -> Function execution.
revision.common_mistakes: Using include for database credentials, causing script to crash silently.

topics.title: Arrays & Strings: Array Functions, String Manipulation & Unicode Processing

intro.definition: Arrays in PHP are ordered hash maps. Strings are byte arrays supported by rich manipulation libraries.
intro.background: All database rows, forms, and sessions are modeled as associative arrays in PHP.
intro.importance: Mastery of array transformations and string sanitization is crucial for backend engineering.
objectives: Filter and map arrays with callbacks.
Tokenize strings with explode and implode.

fundamentals.concepts: Arrays map keys to values. Strings can be manipulated using offset indexing or helper functions.

terminology.definition: Array with custom named string keys.
Splits string by delimiter into array.
Concatenates array elements with a delimiter into string.

fundamentals.principles:
1. Key Uniqueness: Associative array keys must be distinct.
2. Immutable Strings: Operations produce fresh string copies.

sequence: 1. Array initialized with brackets `[]`.
2. Elements added with auto-incremented integer or string keys.
3. array_filter removes elements failing a test predicate.
4. array_map transforms each element.
5. implode formats array into displayable string.

diagram.caption: Figure 2.3: Array Filtering and Formatting Pipeline

important_points: PHP arrays function as ordered hash tables.
explode() splits strings; implode() joins arrays.
asort() preserves associative keys; sort() reindexes.
array_map() transforms elements via callback.
array_filter() extracts matching subsets.

revision.summary: Arrays and strings are core data carriers in PHP. Higher-order functions enable declarative transformations.
revision.mechanisms: Hash lookup -> Callback evaluation -> Array recombination.
revision.common_mistakes: Using sort() on database rows and losing primary key indices.
